title: Beating Ebola takes more than medicine – I saw what worked in west Africa a decade ago | Kayode Akintola
summary: The outbreak in DR Congo is shaping up to be the worst ever, but the support of local faith leaders – and adequate funding – will be needed to bring it under control Ebola is terrifying: I know, because I lived through the world’s worst outbreak of the disease . That was in west Africa between 2013 and 2016, when anyone infected by the virus had a nearly 40% chance of dying . There were 28,600 cases and 11,300 deaths then. Now a rare strain of Ebola is spreading in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, much more quickly than a decade ago in Sierra Leone, Liberia and neighbouring countries. It is the 17th outbreak in DR Congo and already its worst, with more than 5,000 deaths . The UN is warning that the spread of the disease is outstripping the response, and it is widely expected to become the worst Ebola outbreak in history. There is no proven vaccine or treatment yet for the Bundibugyo variant; almost 50% of those infected have died . Continue reading...

title: International UN talks on controlling use of autonomous weapons collapse
summary: Week-long efforts fail to establish negotiating mandate on AI warfare after Russian ‘filibustering’ Week-long efforts to agree a negotiating mandate for a legally binding international treaty to control the use of autonomous weapons collapsed just before 5am after all-night talks failed to overcome Russian objections. Despite an overwhelming majority of states at the UN’s Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) in Geneva wanting to agree a negotiating mandate leading to a legally binding treaty, the need for consensus forced the conference to adopt a much weaker option.
